page: Amazon Web Services r5d.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. This configuration delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, it includes 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the lower tier, as evidenced by weak ratings in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression tests. However, the instance demonstrates average multi-core CPU performance across stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached read/write operations remains consistently in the average tier. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also align with average benchmark expectations.

The r5d.12xlarge offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads requiring high memory density combined with fast local storage, reducing the need for external network-attached storage. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-core processing speed, making it less suitable for single-threaded compute-heavy tasks. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, caching layers, and data processing workloads that benefit from local NVMe SSD temporary storage.
